thread:
elena.docs: Heads-up: rolling out new snippet security & usage guidelines for SDK docs. TL;DR: interactive snippets will be sandboxed, the snippet-linter will block unsafe patterns (no eval, no outbound network calls), and authors must declare required permissions in the frontmatter by May 20. Please read the plan below and flag any blockers. :megaphone:

sam.devex: Nice — any migration help for existing examples?

elena.docs: Yes. We added a migration checklist + automated fixer in the docs repo. Steps: 1) run `docs/snippet-lint --fix` locally, 2) move any external network calls to the examples/fixtures folder or replace with fixtures, 3) add `snippet_permissions` in frontmatter (see examples). We'll run a staged rollout (preview -> stable -> enforce).

nate.sdk: Quick question: are we banning all fetch/http usage inside snippets? Some SDK examples call our internal healthcheck endpoint for demo purposes.

elena.docs: Not banning entirely — runtime calls to external URLs will be disallowed in the interactive runner. For static examples that show an HTTP call, authors should swap to a mocked response or link to the runnable recipe in examples/ if external access is necessary. Internal-only healthcheck calls should be converted to `examples/localhost-mocks` or replaced with a short snippet showing the SDK call + a note about the response.

kate.security: Reviewed the guidelines. We need authors to include a short threat-model line in the frontmatter for any snippet that touches keys, tokens, or file I/O. Also require a `csp` tag for interactive pages. I'll add a template to the security checklist.

elena.docs: Thanks Kate — will add templates. Also: docs CI will report snippet-lint failures as warnings during preview, and as errors in the final enforce stage (target: June 15 enforcement). Preview rollout starts next week (May 1).

docs-bot: snippet-lint v0.9.0 has been added to the docs CI pipeline on branch `docs/snippet-hardening`. Rule highlights: `no-eval`, `no-remote-http-in-interactive`, `require-snippet-permissions`, `no-credentials-in-code`. See https://git.redwood.ai/docs/snippet-lint/v0.9.0 for rule docs.

sam.devex: Will the interactive sandbox still allow iframe->postMessage with a controlled API surface? Some tutorials rely on sending notes back to the playground UI.

elena.docs: Yes — we provide a small postMessage API surface: `{ sendOutput, requestCredentialPrompt }` only. Anything that could trigger network egress or access host filesystem will be rejected by the sandbox runner. We'll publish the API contract and mock helpers next week.

nate.sdk: Migration burden estimate for SDK team: ~8 small samples, 3 that call internal services. I'll schedule time and tag elena/docs for reviews.

elena.docs: Perfect — if any team needs help, drop a PR and use the label `docs-snippet-migration`. We'll prioritize reviews for those.

kate.security: One more ask: update internal training doc with a 5-minute checklist so contributors know the quick wins. I can draft that.

elena.docs: That would be great. I'll put together the rollout calendar and checklist doc in the `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` subsection and ping the repos when preview goes live. Thanks everyone — feel free to @elena.docs with questions. :white_check_mark:
